newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-SCOTLAND AND ZIMBABWE DRAWN TOGETHER IN DUNHILL CUP.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-SCOTLAND AND ZIMBABWE DRAWN TOGETHER IN DUNHILL CUP.

text.p: Holders Scotland and the Zimbabwean team they beat to win last year's Alfred Dunhill Cup were drawn in the same round-robin group on Wednesday for the event starting on Thursday.

They were seeded fifth and fourth respectively among the 16 teams taking part in the 12th edition of this prestigious one million pounds sterling ($1.56 million) tournament and will meet on Saturday after taking on unseeded India and Sweden over the first two days.
"We'll just have to beat them this time," said Zimbabwean captain Nick Price, who hopes to end a barren run of luck with a victory this week with team mates Mark McNulty and Tony Johnstone.
The Scottish team comprises world number two Colin Montgomerie, who has clinched top spot on the European money list for the fourth successive year, Andrew Coltart and newcomer Raymond Russell.

The strong United States team of Phil Mickelson, Mark O'Meara and Steve Stricker, first, fourth and fifth respectively on the U.S. money list, were seeded first with eighth-seeded Spain, England and Italy in their group.
South Africa, led by world number four Ernie Els, are the third seeds and will have to contend with form team Ireland, the sixth seeds, Canada and Wales.
Irishman Darren Clarke won the German Masters on Sunday with team mates Paul McGinley joint fifth and Padraig Harrington joint eighth.
"I haven't played well here at times," Els said. "We've only reached the Sunday semifinals once since I began playing in 1992. I'd like to do better."
Greg Norman, part of the Australian side who won the event in 1985 and 1986, the first two years it was played, will lead the second seeds against seventh seeds New Zealand, Japan and Germany.
Price, the 1994 British Open champion and former world number one, has had problems this year with a sinus condition diagnosed in May.
"I played only five events from May to September. It was disappointing because I had started the year so well. All I needed was for my putting to click into place," he said on Wednesday.
"I've earned $400,000 this year. Most of it came before the end of May.

"With the sinus condition I was always stuffy and had dizzy spells but the worst thing was the fatigue in my legs. I'd play with my kids for half an hour and have to lie down for the rest of the day," he said.
He said he received countless remedies from members of the public. "Some of them looked like they came from an African witch doctor.
"But I didn't use any of them. I saw a new specialist last week and he told me I don't need surgery which is great. But I've had an allergy test to see what causes it."
He expects to get the results of the tests within a week.
Price, a double U.S. PGA champion whose ranking has plunged to 13th this year, is 46th on the U.S. money list which he led in 1993 and 1994.
He accepts that he will not play this month's U.S. Tour Championship, for which a top-30 position is required, after opting against skipping this event to try and qualify for that one.
"To me this is a once-a-year opportunity. I get to play with my old friends at St Andrews. It is pretty special," he said.
